question: With a concurrency group for each Work item on a Run's job, does GitHub keep one Run running and one pending, cancel the older pending Run, and never cancel the one running?
pass: As GitHub documents it (section 6; the working rulings on issue 251, ruling 1): four pushes ten seconds apart to a canary branch start four runs of one workflow whose one job, granted nothing, sleeps ninety seconds under concurrency {group: lane-p44, cancel-in-progress: false}. Read every fifteen seconds until all four have concluded, at no read is more than one run in progress or more than one waiting; each run that waited and was followed by a newer one concludes cancelled without having started; and no run that started is cancelled. Pass if all three hold. The Factory's Run is a dispatch, not a push; a concurrency group applies to a job whatever started its workflow, and the fixture notes the trigger as a difference.

body.principle: The verdict follows the pass condition written before the run, from section 6 and the working rulings on issue 251.
body.workflow:
# Trial P-44 (software-factory, issue 251): one job under a concurrency group, on one branch only. It is granted
# nothing, holds no secret, checks nothing out and caches nothing; it sleeps, so that runs queue behind it.
name: trial-p44
on:
  push:
    branches: [trial/p-44]
    paths: ["p44/**"]
permissions: {}
jobs:
  lane:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    concurrency:
      group: lane-p44
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
      - run: sleep 90
body.trigger: push to a branch; the Factory's Run is a dispatch, and a concurrency group applies to a job whatever started its workflow
body.noted: A run the group cancelled has a job with started_at set and equal to its created time, no runner and no step: the port tells a run that never started by its job's runner and steps, not by started_at.
